goal: Verify that the entire Docker stack starts correctly: FastAPI services respond on /health, MongoDB, Weaviate and RabbitMQ are accessible.
preconditions_global: Docker and docker compose are installed
Repository is cloned and .env file exists (copied from .env.example)
No other process is occupying ports: 8000-8013, 27017, 8080, 5672, 15672

scenarios.title: Start infrastructure containers
scenarios.description: Starts MongoDB, Weaviate and RabbitMQ. These are dependencies for all services — they must be healthy before starting application services.
preconditions: You are in the project root directory (medRAG/)

steps.action: Start infrastructure containers in the background
steps.command: docker compose up -d mongo weaviate rabbitmq
steps.expected_output:
Container medrag-mongo-1 Started
Container medrag-weaviate-1 Started
Container medrag-rabbitmq-1 Started
steps.notes: First run may take 1-2 min (pulling images)

steps.action: Check that all 3 containers have status healthy
steps.expected_output: All three services should show 'healthy' in the STATUS column. If you see 'starting' — wait 30s and retry.
steps.notes: Weaviate starts slower than the others — may need up to 60s

scenarios.expected_outcome: docker compose ps shows mongo, weaviate, rabbitmq with status healthy

scenarios.title: Start application services
scenarios.description: Builds and starts all FastAPI services. Each should expose a /health endpoint.

steps.action: Build and start all application services
steps.command: docker compose up -d --build api-gateway auth admin ingestion parser chunking embedding indexing
steps.expected_output: Each service should appear with status 'Started' or 'Running'
steps.notes: First build takes several minutes (Python dependency installation via uv)

steps.action: Check logs for startup errors
steps.command: docker compose logs --tail=1 api-gateway auth admin ingestion parser chunking embedding indexing
steps.expected_output: Each service should print 'Application startup complete' or 'Uvicorn running on'. Connection errors to MongoDB or RabbitMQ indicate a Docker network issue.
steps.notes: Look for: ERROR, CRITICAL, Connection refused

scenarios.expected_outcome: 8 application services running with no startup errors in logs

scenarios.title: Health check — api-gateway (port 8000)
scenarios.description: The gateway is the entry point for all requests. It must respond first.

steps.action: Call /health on api-gateway
steps.notes: If you get 'Connection refused' — the service has not started. Check: docker compose logs api-gateway

scenarios.title: Health check — auth service (port 8001)
scenarios.description: The auth service must be accessible directly and through the gateway. Also verifies the MongoDB connection.

steps.action: Health check directly on auth service
steps.notes: If auth returns 500 — there is a problem connecting to MongoDB. Check: docker compose logs auth

scenarios.title: Health check — all remaining services (ports 8007–8013)
scenarios.description: Verifies that each service starts and responds correctly on /health.

steps.action: Health check admin service
Health check ingestion service
Health check parser service (RabbitMQ worker — only /health, no business HTTP routes)
steps.notes: Parser is a RabbitMQ worker — it has no business endpoints, only /health

steps.action: Health check chunking service
Health check embedding service (may start slowly — loads BGE-m3 model)
steps.notes: Embedding loads the sentence-transformers model on startup. May need 60-120s on first run. If 'starting', wait and retry.

steps.action: Health check indexing service
Health check eval service

scenarios.title: Weaviate — readiness and schema
scenarios.description: Weaviate must be ready to accept vectors. Check the ready endpoint and that the schema is accessible.

steps.action: Check if Weaviate is ready
steps.expected_output: Empty response with HTTP 200 — Weaviate is ready
steps.notes: If you get 503 — Weaviate is still starting. Wait 30s.

steps.action: Fetch current schema (may be empty on first start)
steps.notes: The 'Chunk' class appears only after the first ingestion pipeline run. At this stage classes=[] is correct.

scenarios.expected_outcome: Weaviate responds 200 on /ready and returns valid schema JSON

scenarios.title: RabbitMQ — Management UI and queues
scenarios.description: Verify that RabbitMQ is alive, the broker is accessible through the Management API, and required queues have been declared by services.

steps.action: Open RabbitMQ Management UI in browser
steps.expected_output: RabbitMQ login page. Login: guest, password: guest.
steps.notes: On macOS 'open' launches the browser. On Linux use: xdg-open or enter the URL manually.

steps.action: Check queue list via Management API
steps.expected_output: List of queues. Expected: parser.queue, chunking.queue, embedding.queue, indexing.queue, eval.queue
steps.notes: Queues are declared by services on startup. If the list is empty — services have not yet connected to RabbitMQ. Check: docker compose logs parser chunking

steps.action: Check that the 'documents' exchange exists
steps.notes: The 'documents' exchange should be of type 'topic' and durable. If 404 — services have not declared the topology.

steps.action: Check that queues have no stuck messages
steps.command: curl -s -u guest:guest 'http://localhost:15672/api/queues/%2F/parser.queue' | python3 -c "import sys,json; q=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'messages: {q[\"messages\"]}, ready: {q[\"messages_ready\"]}, unacked: {q[\"messages_unacknowledged\"]}')"
steps.notes: On a clean start queues should be empty. If messages > 0 — may be leftovers from a previous session.

scenarios.expected_outcome: Queues exist, 'documents' exchange exists, queues are empty

scenarios.title: Stop the stack
scenarios.description: Clean shutdown of all containers. Data is preserved in volumes.

steps.action: Stop all containers (preserve volumes with data)
steps.notes: MongoDB, Weaviate and RabbitMQ data is in named volumes — survives restart

steps.action: If you want to wipe ALL data (fresh start)
steps.notes: WARNING: -v removes volumes — you will lose all data in MongoDB and Weaviate. Use only for a fresh start.
